title: DeepInfer column: the other end of inference
deck: Strata runs a large model on one machine. DeepSeek's DeepInfer lets hundreds of GPUs serve a huge number of users together. The same ideas, done on a cluster.

pages.title: The other end: how DeepSeek runs inference on a cluster
pages.deck: What DeepInfer is, which part was open-sourced, what parts the production system is made of, and how it differs from Strata.

pages.title: Wide expert parallelism: spreading experts across 64 GPUs
pages.deck: Attention uses data parallelism. Experts use expert parallelism over 64–128 GPUs, so each GPU reads fewer experts per step. Then EPLB copies popular experts to even out the busiest GPU.

pages.title: E/P/D disaggregation and the 72-hour KV cache
pages.deck: The vision encoder, prefill and decode are deployed separately. The KV cache goes into a dedicated 3FS cluster and is read back on a hit. If SWA is missing, only the last short stretch of tokens is replayed.

pages.title: DSpark speculative decoding and zero-overhead scheduling
pages.deck: Drafts guess 5 tokens at once, confidence decides how many to verify, and the CPU prepares the next batch one step ahead so the GPU never stops.

pages.title: Batch invariance, deterministic sampling and structured outputs
pages.deck: Put the same request next to different batch neighbors, and the order of a floating-point sum can change. DeepInfer pins down both the summation order and the random numbers, then uses a bitmask so the model emits only a legal format.
